title: High School Contexts and STEM Career Pathways: Math Self-Efficacy, Teacher Diversity, and Student–Teacher Race Matching
abstract: Guided by Social Cognitive Career Theory, this study examined how relational and structural school contexts were associated with postsecondary STEM major choice. Using nationally representative, time-lagged data from ELS:2002, we tested whether student–teacher racial matching in high school was linked to STEM major selection 4 years later through math self-efficacy, math achievement, and perceptions of student–teacher relationships, while accounting for school-level teacher racial diversity. Multilevel structural equation modeling showed that racial matching was not directly associated with STEM major choice but was indirectly associated through math achievement, including a serial pathway through math self-efficacy and achievement. Teacher racial diversity was positively associated with STEM major selection and moderated the math self-efficacy–STEM choice association. Exploratory analyses indicated that the racial-matching association with STEM major choice varied across racial/ethnic groups. Findings highlight the importance of integrating interpersonal and institutional contexts in understanding STEM pathway development.
